sources.entry: Pullo - Your GitHub pull requests and Actions runs in the MacBook notch, with alerts when CI fails, a PR is approved or a review is requested.

summary.one_liner: Pullo is a free, open-source macOS app that shows your GitHub pull requests and GitHub Actions runs in the notch, with alerts for CI results, approvals and review requests.
summary.what_it_does: Pullo displays your GitHub pull requests and GitHub Actions runs in a panel that slides out of the MacBook notch (or the top center of the menu bar on Macs without a notch). It sends alerts when CI results come in, a PR is approved, a comment is posted, or a review is requested. The Actions view shows running, waiting-for-approval and failed runs, with deploys one click away. Opening a run shows each job and step live, and you can re-run failed work, cancel stuck runs, or open the log on GitHub. You can create custom tabs for PRs and runs using GitHub search syntax, and add several accounts, each with its own list. The app talks directly to the GitHub API from the Mac, borrowing the token from the GitHub CLI (gh) and not storing it.
use_cases: Watch CI results without opening a browser
Get alerted when a pull request is approved or needs my review
Re-run or cancel a GitHub Actions workflow from the Mac
Track deploys and running workflows at a glance
Monitor PRs across several GitHub accounts
how_to_run: Download Pullo.dmg and drag Pullo to Applications.
Run: brew install gh && gh auth login
Open Pullo and hover over the notch.
stack: Swift (macOS app, inferred from macOS 14+ and Liquid Glass)
notable: Lives in the MacBook notch and slides out alerts, then gets out of the way
Borrows the token from gh and never stores it; no server or sign-up
Custom tabs written with GitHub search syntax
Supports multiple accounts, each with its own list
Re-run, cancel, and live step-by-step view of Actions jobs
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or later and Apple silicon
Needs the GitHub CLI (gh) installed and logged in
Beta features are opt-in via Settings → Updates
